comments.body:
## OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-05: REMOVE the field

The operator ruled: remove `CodeHealthConfig.enabled`, consistent with the dce2 ruling on the
inert `analyzers` field.

I raised the counter-argument when presenting the choice — that this differs from dce2 because
deleting `analyzers` removed a knob that never did anything, whereas deleting `enabled` removes
the only advertised OFF SWITCH for the whole code-health subsystem. The operator considered it
and chose removal. Recording that the tradeoff was surfaced and knowingly accepted.

Scope: remove the field, its coercion row, and its config-surface entries (including the
`REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` env var), and ensure the docs no longer advertise an off switch
that does not exist.

Follow dce2's landed precedent for the mechanics — it is the template: dce2 also had to add a
warn-class TOMBSTONE for the removed key, because `test_config_surface_golden.py` fails the
build when a golden-pinned key exists in neither the live schema nor the tombstone registry. A
still-set key must WARN and exit 0, not be silently dropped. Expect the same requirement here,
and check whether removing this field orphans a coercion helper the way dce2 orphaned
`_as_str_dict`.

The guard AC (preventing silent regression to inert) is moot for a deleted field, but note it
depends on bug 2c58-e710-275e-4ff7 anyway — the current gate could never have caught this
field, because `.enabled` is read on other configs.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`CodeHealthConfig.enabled` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:538`, default `False`) has ZERO read
sites in `src/rebar`. Nothing gates on it.

A code trace of the live path confirms it: `_commands/metrics.py:139-148` loads
`config.load_config(root).code_health` and carries only `scan_roots` (:144), `size_cap` (:145) and
`size_near_fraction` (:146) into the metrics context. `enabled` is never consulted, so the
structural metrics (`module_size_distribution`, `oversized_module_count`, `complexity_summary`,
`duplication_summary`) evaluate even at the default `enabled=False`.

The field is documented and settable, so an operator can set `enabled = false` and reasonably
believe code-health analysis is off. It is not.

## Why it was never caught

The 6754 inert-config gate cannot see this one -- see the sibling bug on that gate. It matches
bare attribute NAMES globally, and `.enabled` is read on other configs (`ui.enabled`,
`LangfuseConfig`, under `llm/`), so this field passes without ever being read itself. That is also
why it carries no `# read-via:` marker while the neighbouring `analyzers` field needed one.

## The decision this needs

Same shape as dce2: either HONOR the flag (gate structural metric evaluation on it) or DELETE it.
Honoring it is a behavioral change -- metrics that run today would stop running for anyone on the
default -- so this needs an explicit operator ruling, not an agent's judgment.

Note the interaction with dce2's ruling: the operator chose to DELETE the inert `analyzers` field
rather than wire it, with intent preserved as idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2. A consistent ruling here
is plausible but must not be assumed, because the two differ -- deleting `analyzers` removes a knob
that never did anything, whereas deleting `enabled` removes the only advertised off switch for the
whole code-health subsystem.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An explicit operator decision is recorded: honor `enabled` or remove it.
- [ ] If HONORED: structural metric evaluation is gated on it, with a test proving the metrics do
      NOT evaluate at `enabled=False` and DO at `enabled=True`; the default's behavior change is
      called out in the changelog.
- [ ] If REMOVED: the field, its coercion row and its config-surface entries go, and the docs no
      longer advertise an off switch that does not exist.
- [ ] Either way, a guard prevents it silently regressing to inert again (this depends on the 6754
      gate fix -- a same-named field cannot be policed until that lands).

## Provenance

Found by a code-trace archaeology pass over the metrics/code-health system while scoping dce2.

## Operator ruling — RECORDED

**Decision: REMOVE `CodeHealthConfig.enabled`.** Ruled by the operator on 2026-08-05 and
recorded as the first comment on this ticket ("OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-05: REMOVE the
field", author `RebarBotNava`, `author_id` `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`) — that comment is the
citable attestation this AC closes against.

The counter-argument was surfaced to the operator before the ruling: this differs from dce2
because deleting `analyzers` removed a knob that never did anything, whereas deleting
`enabled` removes the only advertised OFF SWITCH for the whole code-health subsystem. The
operator considered that tradeoff and chose removal knowingly. This is a one-way door for the
advertised switch; the intent it expressed is not being preserved as a follow-up idea (unlike
dce2, whose analyzer-dispatch intent survives as idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2) because there is no
surviving design for a code-health off switch — re-adding one later would be a fresh feature
decision, not a restoration. Do not re-litigate the ruling.

## Fix plan (REMOVAL, per the recorded operator ruling above)

Pure removal — the field controls nothing today (zero read sites), so deleting it cannot
change what runs.

1. `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — delete the `enabled: bool = False` field from
   `CodeHealthConfig`; delete its `"enabled": lambda v, k: _as_bool(v, k)` coercion row from
   the `code_health` entry of `_SECTIONS`; refresh the class docstring, which no longer
   describes an inert-by-default toggle.
2. `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — add TWO warn-class tombstones to `_TOMBSTONE_REGISTRY` so a
   still-set input WARNs and exits 0 rather than being silently dropped: an `env` tombstone for
   `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` and a `cfg` tombstone for `code_health.enabled`. This is
   mandatory, not optional: `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` fails the build when a
   golden-pinned key exists in neither the live schema nor the tombstone registry.
3. `docs/config.md` — drop `enabled` from both TOML examples and from the prose type list in
   the `code_health.*` section (so the docs stop advertising an off switch that does not
   exist), and add both tombstoned inputs to the warn-class list.
4. `tests/unit/test_code_health_config.py` — drop only the plain `value.enabled is False` /
   `value.enabled is True` assertions from the two happy-path tests.
5. `tests/unit/test_code_health_config_heldout.py` — drop the `-c code_health.enabled=true`
   CLI override argument, the `enabled` entries in the composed config/sources assertions, and
   `code_health.enabled` / `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` from the golden-surface expectation
   sets.
6. `tests/scripts/test_metrics_docs.py` — drop `enabled` from the documented-keys tuple.
7. `tests/unit/test_config_backcompat.py` — add a RUNTIME test (the home of the existing
   tombstone/warn tests) asserting the new tombstones actually fire: loading a config with
   `[code_health] enabled = true` set, and separately with `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` set,
   emits the warn-class removed-input message and does NOT raise (warn class, not error
   class). Registry presence alone is not proof — the warn path is verified by execution.

Not touched: `tests/golden/config_surface.json` stays pinned (that is the point of the golden
— the tombstones, not a golden edit, account for the removed entries).

`_as_bool` is NOT orphaned by this removal (dozens of other coercion rows in `_SECTIONS` use
it), unlike dce2's `_as_str_dict`.

### How the removal is proved

- `grep -rn "code_health.enabled\|REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED" src/rebar` returns nothing.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py tests/unit/test_config_backcompat.py
  tests/unit/test_code_health_config.py tests/unit/test_code_health_config_heldout.py` passes.
- `rebar config validate` with the key still set exits 0 and reports it as a removed input.

### Evidence of no behavior change

`rebar metrics` before and after produces the same structural metrics (`module_size_distribution`,
`oversized_module_count`, `complexity_summary`, `duplication_summary`). A byte-identical whole-output
diff is NOT achievable — two consecutive runs already differ in time- and store-driven ticket metrics
(dce2 found the same) — so the evidence is per-metric attribution over the code_health lens.

### On the guard AC

MOOT for a deleted field: there is nothing left to regress to inert. It also depended on bug
2c58-e710-275e-4ff7 regardless — the current inert-config gate could never have caught this
field, because `.enabled` is read on other configs (`ui.enabled`, `LangfuseConfig`).

stop advertising an off switch; document the tombstones

runtime test that the new warn-class tombstones fire and do not raise
